Figure caption: Key milestones in LNP-enabled genetic medicines (2017–2024), from high-throughput LNP discovery to first-in-human genome editing and scalable manufacturing.

Figure caption: (A) Schematic of a conventional LNP and a ligand-targeted LNP in which a surface ligand is presented on PEG lipids to enable receptor-mediated uptake. (B) Representative ionizable lipids (DLin-MC3-DMA, ALC-0315, SM-102) and helper lipids (DSPC, DOPE).

Figure caption: Representative methods for LNP fabrication: (A) bulk mixing approaches (thin-film hydration, solvent injection, bulk nanoprecipitation, melting emulsification); (B) microfluidic approaches using mixer designs such as T-junction, hydrodynamic flow focusing, staggered herringbone, ring-type, Tesla, and baffle mixers. Adapted from Ref. [104] under a CC BY ND 4.0 license (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/).

Figure caption: Formulation, synthesis, and characterization of programmable RNA–LNPs. (a) Design–assemble–characterize–learn loop linking mixing physics and composition to critical quality attributes. (b) Practical route selection for assembly (bulk, microfluidic, or CIJ/μMIVM) with the key knobs shared across methods. Abbreviations:N/P, amine (nitrogen)–to–phosphate charge ratio; PEG, poly(ethylene glycol); SORT, Selective Organ Targeting (lipid); FRR, flow-rate ratio; Re, Reynolds number; PDI, polydispersity index; TFF, tangential flow filtration; EtOH, ethanol; CQA(s), critical quality attribute(s); ζ-potential, zeta potential; EE, encapsulation efficiency; pKa, apparent acid dissociation constant; CIJ, confined impinging-jet (mixer); μMIVM, micro multi-inlet vortex mixer; LPH, liters per hour; ms, milliseconds; unit ops, unit operations.

Figure caption: (A) LNPs can package diverse cargos (pDNA, mRNA/circRNA, ASO, miRNA/siRNA, and CRISPR components). (B) After i.v. dosing, therapeutics face off-target biodistribution, immune clearance, serum nucleases, and extravasation. (C) Inside cells, uptake is followed by potential recycling vs endosomal escape; cytosolic cargos act via translation or RISC, whereas others (pDNA, Cas-gRNA, HDR templates) require nuclear entry. Adapted from Ref. [123] under a CC BY 4.0 license (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
